properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.82.0): add_change_event asks DrawnEdges::classify whether each CHANGED edge is already there, reports it as edges_already_present, and re-creates it anyway with `{action}` alone; create_edge REPLACES, so the acceptance set_artifact_checksum put on the edge (accepted_baseline, accepted_seq, checksum_after) is erased — the revise contract held for node properties by upsert_node was never held for an edge another tool decorates
properties.source: who:ajs via the dev_reflow2 hub session, on the hosted design (api.flo2.io/g/reflow2, reflow2 0.81.1)
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-11, on the observation below.

1 OBSERVED (0.81.1, hosted): add_change_event chg:… with six affected → set_artifact_checksums on two of them (applied; the next copy showed accepted_baseline true, accepted_seq, checksum_after on both CHANGED edges) → add_change_event again, same id, affected extended by one artifact (reply: edges_already_present ×6, edges_drawn ×1) → the next copy: both edges carried {accepted_baseline: false, action: modified} only; reflow2_check failed on those two files. Re-accepting restored them.

2 PRECEDENT: fact:root-cause-the-revise-contract-is-implemented-per-handler-and-guarded-by-instances-2026-09-28 (the class "a revise keeps what it was not passed", fixed for NODE properties by upsert_node and the class test a_revise_keeps_what_it_was_not_passed.rs) and fact:a-checksum-accepted-against-a-change-that-does-not-name-the-artifact-is-applied-and-does-not-count-2026-10-07 (its sibling, which made the two together a trap: name the artifact or the acceptance does not count; name it afterwards and the others are erased).

3 CANDIDATES: C1 the handler ignores classify's answer and re-draws with {action}; C2 the core's create_edge replaces an existing edge's properties instead of merging; C3 (outside) the hosted path — the gateway's _meta rewrite or the copy's import/export round trip — dropped the properties; C4 (outside) a duplicate CHANGED edge carried the acceptance and the revise removed it.

4 MEASUREMENTS: C3 REFUTED — reproduced on a scratch store with the PUBLISHED 0.82.0 binary through the --call door, no gateway, no copy: after accept {accepted_baseline: true, accepted_seq: 1, checksum_after: sha256:…}; after the revise {accepted_baseline: false, action: modified}. C4 REFUTED — one CHANGED edge per (event, artifact) in every copy; edge identity is (type, from, to). C1 CONFIRMED — crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/temporal_tools.rs ~:929-941: `edges.classify(…)?;` with the bool discarded (its own doc: "Returns whether it was already there, so a caller can skip a redundant write"), then unconditional g.create_edge(… Props::new().set("action", action)). Of the four classify callers, only add_capability (capture.rs ~:2181) honours the answer. C2 CONFIRMED as the mechanism — the post-revise edge carried accepted_baseline FALSE, a schema default a replace-write produces, not the stored true.

5 CAUSE: C1 riding on C2. The revise contract is held one level too shallow — for node properties, not for an edge another tool decorates. CHANGED is the one edge in the design another tool decorates (set_artifact_checksum's stamp_acceptance / accept_changed_edge write onto it), so add_change_event is the only writer where the class bites; record_finding's CAUSES re-draw has the same shape but its only property comes from the same call.

6 FIX (PR fix/a-revised-affected-list-keeps-the-acceptances-on-its-changed-edges): when classify says the edge is present, add_change_event reads the stored edge's properties and carries every one the call did not pass; only `action` moves. Pinned by tests/a_revised_affected_list_keeps_the_acceptances_on_its_changed_edges.rs: 2 of 3 failed on unchanged main (the precondition passed), 3 of 3 pass with the change, the neighbouring class tests stay green.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the hosted gateway path adds anything of its own — unnecessary for this defect once it reproduced locally, and not measured separately. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
